ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating KL-Regularized Fine-Tuning for Diffusion Models
PROPOSAL: We will implement Kl Rosenberg's KL-regularized PPO algorithm, modified for diffusion models, using the DM-Fubra model as the pre-trained reference and the CIFAR-10 dataset for fine-tuning. We will compare the results with a baseline of plain PPO optimization without KL regularization.
CONTROLS: DM-Fubra model without fine-tuning as an ablation, setting the KL coefficient to zero to demonstrate the importance of KL regularization.
COST: 3000
PREDICTION: KL regularization will improve stability of training but may under-regularize the model, causing the fine-tuned model to generate samples that are too dissimilar from the reference distribution. This could lead to slightly better performance in terms of in-distribution samples, but potentially worse performance on out-of-distribution samples.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluating the Effectiveness of Trajectory KL-Divergence for Diffusion Models
PROPOSAL: We will expand on the previous proposal by experimenting with different variants of the trajectory KL divergence relaxation, such as substituting the reverse process with a learned prior or integrating it with entropy regularization. We will use the U-Net model as the pre-trained reference and evaluate fine-tuning performance on the image-like tasks (text-to-image generation, document layout generation) using the LSUN, COCO, and Gram data augmentation datasets.
CONTROLS: Comparing with and without entropy regularization, and using different numbers of denoising steps while computing the KL divergence.
COST: 6500
PREDICTION: The trajectory KL divergence relaxation might improve performance on tasks with complex, high-variance outputs, but its effectiveness on low-variance tasks (e.g., molecule generation) is uncertain. We may see inconsistent results across different datasets and tasks due to the sensitivity of the KL relaxation to hyperparameters.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Fine-Tuning Diffusion Models via Reward-Driven Rejection Sampling
PROPOSAL: We will implement the RSO (Reward-Driven Rejection Sampling) algorithm for fine-tuning diffusion models, using the Learned Dipole method as the rejection sampling component. We will evaluate its performance on generating high-quality documents and images, using the APPearl (dataset) datasets.
CONTROLS: Directly comparing the performance of RSO with that of KL-regularized PPO (from Proposal 1) to understand the trade-offs between regularization and reward-driven sampling.
COST: 9000
PREDICTION: RSO should outperform KL-regularized PPO on tasks with high-magnitude rewards, such as document layout generation, due to its ability to learn a more direct mapping between rewards and sampling decisions. However, it may struggle with tasks where accurate sampling probabilities are difficult to compute, such as complex image generation, and require careful tuning of the rejection threshold to achieve competitive results.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: Refining Fine-Tuning Diffusion Models via Reward-Driven Rejection Sampling (Proposal 3)
PROPOSAL: As before, we will implement the RSO (Reward-Driven Rejection Sampling) algorithm for fine-tuning diffusion models, but we will also extend it by introducing a 'softmax' over Höft-beam widths, so a late output based on blurring output samples around "better fitted" forward paths is incorporated - and use these modifications on molecule generation (GA dataset, ZINC database) and text-to-image tasks (CIFAR-10, LSUN).
CONTROLS: Including a version of RSO without the added softmax filter as a baseline to demonstrate the improvement of the modified rejection sampling strategy.
COST: 10800
PREDICTION: The incorporation of the softmax filter should bring RSO's performance on molecule generation and text-to-image tasks more in line with that of KL-regularized PPO, especially on tasks where accurate sampling probabilities are difficult to compute. However, it may introduce some numerical instability due to the behavior of the softmax function.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: Improving Diffusion Model Fine-Tuning with Trajectory KL-Divergence (Proposal 2)
PROPOSAL: As before, we will experiment with different variants of the trajectory KL divergence relaxation, but with an additional focus on correcting the initial value function bias by incorporating a learned prior that approximates the initial noise distribution.
CONTROLS: Evaluating performance with and without the learned prior, and comparing with KL-regularized PPO and RSO.
COST: 8300
PREDICTION: The correction of the initial value function bias should lead to improved performance on tasks where the pre-trained model's initial noise distribution is significantly different from the target distribution. However, it may also introduce additional computational overhead due to the need to learn an additional prior.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Exploring Fine-Tuning for Pre-Trained Flow Models Without Explicit Rewards
PROPOSAL: We will focus on correcting the errors in pre-trained flow models by fine-tuning them using only samples from the data distribution, without explicit rewards. We will use a combination of KL regularization and self-supervised reconstruction objectives to guide the fine-tuning process.
CONTROLS: Comparing the performance of the fine-tuned flow models with a pre-trained model as a baseline, and evaluating different combinations of KL regularization and reconstruction objectives.
COST: 13500
PREDICTION: The proposed approach should be able to correct the errors in pre-trained flow models, especially in tasks with significant discretization and statistical errors, but may require careful tuning of hyperparameters and may not always achieve state-of-the-art results.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Improving Flow Model Fine-Tuning with Flow-Constrained KL-Divergence
PROPOSAL: We will extend the Proposal 4 by incorporating flow constraints into the KL divergence computation to make it flow-invariant, allowing for more accurate comparison between the pre-trained and fine-tuned models. We will use a flow-constrained KL divergence upper bound that takes into account the Jacobian determinant of the flow transformation.
CONTROLS: Evaluating the performance of the flow-constrained KL divergence with and without flow constraints, and comparing with the standard KL divergence.
COST: 15450
PREDICTION: The flow-constrained KL divergence should lead to improved performance on tasks where the flow model's transformation is significantly nonlinear or has a complex Jacobian determinant, such as molecule generation and text-to-image tasks, but may be computationally expensive due to the need to compute the Jacobian determinant.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating the Impact of Generative Structure on Fine-Tuning Diffusion Models
PROPOSAL: We will analyze the generative structure of diffusion models and its impact on fine-tuning performance. We will decompose the diffusion process into smaller sub-processes and fine-tune each sub-process separately using various objectives, including KL regularization and self-supervised reconstruction objectives.
CONTROLS: Evaluating the performance of the fine-tuned models with and without separate sub-process fine-tuning, and comparing with pre-trained models.
COST: 17000
PREDICTION: The fine-tuning of individual sub-processes should lead to improved performance on tasks where the diffusion process has a complex generative structure, such as molecule generation and text-to-image tasks, but may also introduce additional computational overhead due to the need to fine-tune multiple sub-processes.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: A Theoretical Analysis of KL-Regularization for Diffusion Models
PROPOSAL: We will provide a theoretical analysis of the KL-regularization term used in diffusion model fine-tuning, focusing on its convergence properties and implications for the generalization performance of the fine-tuned model. We will derive convergence bounds for the KL-regularized objective and analyze its behavior in both batch and online settings.
CONTROLS: Proving the convergence of the KL-regularized objective without explicit regularization oversights and identifying the key factors influencing convergence rates.
COST: 19500
PREDICTION: The theoretical analysis should provide insights into the properties of KL-regularization and its implications for diffusion model fine-tuning, but may also reveal some limitations and challenges in applying KL-regularization to real-world tasks.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Experimental Evaluation of Fine-Tuning Methods on Text-to-Image and Document Layout Generation Tasks
PROPOSAL: We will conduct an experimental evaluation of the fine-tuning methods proposed in previous studies on text-to-image and document layout generation tasks, using real-world datasets (e.g. COCO, LayoutLM). We will compare the performance of different fine-tuning methods, including KL-regularized PPO, RSO, and flow-constrained KL divergence, on these tasks.
CONTROLS: Directly comparing the performance of different fine-tuning methods and evaluating the impact of different hyperparameters and settings on fine-tuning performance.
COST: 22650
PREDICTION: The experimental evaluation should provide a comprehensive understanding of the relative strengths and weaknesses of different fine-tuning methods on text-to-image and document layout generation tasks, and help identify the most effective approaches for real-world applications.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE:  Integral-Wise KL-Regularized Diffusion Fine-Tuning
PROPOSAL:  In this experiment, we employ a Monte Carlo (MC) approximation of the marginal KL divergence. We define a set of intermediate checkpoints within the diffusion process and perform MC sampling to approximate the empirical KL divergence between these checkpoints. The pre-trained diffusion model is then fine-tuned using the KL-regularized reward maximization objective, with the approximate marginal KL computed at each iteration. This method will be compared to the variants that fully ignore the KL term and those with the trajectory KL constraint.
CONTROLS:  Kl-regularized reward maximization without any KL term, Trajectory KL constraint, and other recent fine-tuning methods such as RSO and RAFT
COST:  4500
PREDICTION:  This method should achieve more stable training than ignoring the KL term and outperform the subpar results obtained with the trajectory KL constraint, but may suffer from an increased variance due to MC sampling; we expect that with more MC samples, the performance would approach that of the method with exact marginal KL computation, but this might come with increased computational cost per iteration.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE:  Diffusion-Flow MAC (Middle Point Aggregation for Conditional) 
PROPOSAL:  This experiment explores leveraging the intermediates generated by the diffusion and flow processes for efficient fine-tuning. The idea is to use the sequentially generated noisy states as anchor points for amortized likelihood-based adaptation, i.e., via a learned probabilistic conditioner that identifies the important aspects of the noisy states. We approximate the target un-normalized densities using learned components, which should learn the typical set of states sampled along the diffusion and flow trajectories. This would potentially lower the variance of the KL divergence approximation and better adapt the pre-trained model's distribution to the target class.
CONTROLS:  Integral-Wise KL-Regularized Diffusion Fine-Tuning (proposed in the previous turn), PPO adaptation methods without explicit KL regularization, and some recent unconditional flow models trained on generating specific datasets.
COST:  5400
PREDICTION:  The MAC module may converge to a specific KL-optimal adaptation mode in which the conditioner learns to sample states along the trajectories of the pre-trained model that are closer to the target data distribution; in favorable cases, this could enable refinement with a reduction in the number of fine-tuning samples needed, but over-reliance on the intermediate noise might result in model variability unacceptable to downstream users.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE:  Revised Diffusion-Flow MAC (Middle Point Aggregation for Conditional)
PROPOSAL:  In this revised experiment, Diffusion-Flow MAC is extended to a more sophisticated inference strategy that effectively removes the need for per-iteration KL estimation and gives a risk-control strategy at once, borrowing from amortized variational inference ideas. This extended MAC (e-MAC) adds a soft process on top of the traditional MAC per-iteration, moving the entire distribution's learning of KL regularizer off to the conditioner, such that at any given point the conditions benefit of learning forward control to the actual target un-normalized distribution which guides understood distribution direction.
CONTROLS:  Original Diffusion-Flow MAC, Integral-Wise KL-Regularized Diffusion Fine-Tuning, A couple of competitive amortized variational inference approaches for relaxing variational objectives via second order methods.
COST:  7200
PREDICTION:  With e-MAC, the conditioning mechanism might be less prone to under-distribution or over-distribution when doing latter KL's objective, entailing potentially better versatility in correcting non-distribution continuation from pre-learned decision-making principles, though checking the auto-regression-built schedule and prompts or tendency for working whose better under sub-tasks (potentially affected by cut-down variance loss constants) still has lot more worth considering.

TITLE:  e-MAC-based Latent Space Regularization
PROPOSAL:  This experiment applies the extended MAC (e-MAC) to aid the fine-tuning process by dynamically inducing a loss term that arbitrates model uncertainty in the latent space, with the ultimate goal of pruning the model's variability through supplied notions.

PROPOSAL:  This experiment applies the extended MAC (e-MAC) to aid the fine-tuning process by dynamically inducing a loss term that arbitrates model uncertainty in the latent space, with the ultimate goal of pruning the model's variability through supplied notions.
CONTROLS:  Previous experiments based on Diffusion-Flow MAC, Kl-regularized reward maximization without any KL term, and Trajectory KL constraint

ACTION: ADD
TITLE:  Integrated Stochastic Denoising with e-MAC 
PROPOSAL:  This experiment investigates a new fine-tuning strategy that explores integrating stochastic denoising and the extended MAC (e-MAC) within a unified learning framework. The main objective is to identify a promising set of intermediate states for the e-MAC to condition on during the denoising process. We hypothesize that by leveraging both stochastic denoising and conditional modeling, the model can reap benefits from the original objectives while dynamically adjusting its intermediate distributions.
CONTROLS:  Previous experiments based on Diffusion-Flow MAC, kl-regularized reward maximization, and e-MAC-based latent space regularization.
COST:  16200
PREDICTION:  The integrated strategy may provide a more versatile fine-tuning framework that leverages both the strengths of stochastic denoising and e-MAC, potentially reducing overfitting and improving adaptability; however, fine-tuning and learning schedules might need re-examination, and potentially, an unpredictable additional variance rise.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Active Learning for Noisy Labels withHistogram-based Uncertainty Sampling
PROPOSAL: We propose an active learning approach to identify the most uncertain instances with noisy labels. We treat each instance's confidence as a multinomial distribution over its predicted class probabilities, and compute a histogram-based entropy measure. TITLE: Provable Bounds for Cascade Speculative Decoding with Training-Free Self-Speculative Techniques
PROPOSAL: We establish a theoretical framework for analyzing the performance of cascade speculative decoding with training-free self-speculative techniques, providing provable bounds on the expected walltime improvement and the quality of the generated text. We employ a combination of techniques from combinatorial optimization and measure concentration to derive the bounds, which hold under various assumptions about the self-speculative methods and the characteristics of the input sequences. Our results show that the efficiency of the cascade depends crucially on the dimensionality of the sequence space, the strength of the self-speculative methods, and the Rao-Nirenberg distance between the input distribution and the space of possible draft sequences.
CONTROLS: Non-asymptotic estimates of the Rabbat-Tropp-Dictatorship set,, estimation measures of problems in uncertainty quantification.
COST: 270
PREDICTION: We anticipate that the proposed bounds will provide valuable insights into the potential benefits and limitations of cascade speculative decoding with training-free self-speculative techniques, and will help to refine the design of the adaptive scheduling strategy and the cascade architecture. However, we may face challenges in translating the theoretical results into practical solutions, especially when dealing with highly irregular input distributions or strong long-range dependencies in the input sequences.

TITLE: Proposal 3: Heteroscedastic Meta-Reward Learning for Absolute Quality Judgments
PROPOSAL: We propose a Heteroscedastic Meta-Reward Learning approach to address the challenges of absolute quality judgments in LLM-based systems. ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Contextualized Knowledge Utilization via Contrastive Learning
PROPOSAL: Employ contrastive learning to develop a contextualized signal for knowledge utilization, leveraging the idea that if a response is grounded in retrieved context, similar context-all responses will receive higher similarity scores when paired with the target context. The signal of contextualized knowledge utilization E(a|d) can be derived from the mutual information or Jensen-Shannon divergence between outputs of the two encoders.

PROPOSAL: We propose a contrastive learning approach to learn an effective external context utilization metric, inspired by the successful self-supervised methods in computer vision. We design a contrastive loss function that pairs contextual embeddings with both positive (contextually relevant) and negative (irrelevant or contextually incorrect) samples, and train a neural network to maximize the similarity between contextually relevant embeddings and minimize the similarity between contextually irrelevant embeddings. We hypothesize that this approach will improve the robustness and generalizability of our utilization metric across different domains and tasks.

TITLE: Addressing Training Instability through Multi-Modal Augmented Denoising
PROPOSAL: We introduce a novel training framework that addresses instability caused by mismatched cross-modal dynamics in chained multi-modal reasoning. TITLE: Image-Text Curriculum Learning for Multi-Modal Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
PROPOSAL: We introduce a novel training procedure called Image-Text Curriculum Learning, where we progressively increase the difficulty of tasks in a curriculum of reasoning-driven text-to-image generation, instruction-based image editing, and visual question answering. This allows the model to adapt to complex reasoning requirements while learning to reason and reason cohesively across text and vision. By iteratively increasing the difficulty of the tasks, the model learns to integrate complex visual and textual intermediates, promoting more stable and coherent multi-modal reasoning.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Enhanced Intrinsic Process Reward Design for Multi-Turn Agentic Search
PROPOSAL: 
We propose to compute a dense process reward for each interaction turn by comparing the LM's generated text against the learnt mask-based representation of the tools' response. This representation is learned through a self-supervised object detector-style task on the relevant search snippets. The reward for each turn is then calculated as the cosine similarity between the two vectors, making it an intrinsic and domain-agnostic process reward.

PROPOSAL: We propose SparseTrack, a few-shot adaptation method for Sparse Perception Models (SPMs) to novel cameras using a factorized 3D keypoint-based representation. TITLE: Research Questions Answered
We have addressed the research questions by proposing a set of experiments and theoretical results that aim to improve the pre-training of Sparse Perception Models (SPMs) on unlabeled multi-view driving data. Our experiments focus on four main directions:

1. Self-supervised pre-training for SPMs using augmented sparse queries (QueryAugment).

PROPOSAL: We propose a novel query-based Gaussian Splatting pre-training method for Sparse Perception Models. This approach utilizes Gaussian Splatting for explicit scene representation, effectively exploiting unlabeled driving data for pre-training. Specifically, our method renders a 3D scene using a sparse set of implicit queries, and predicts Gaussian parameters for each query, while aggregating visual features using a sparse set of queries. We compare this approach with existing pre-training methods for dense BEV or volumetric representations, and assess its performance on various sparse 3D object detection and occupancy prediction tasks.

TITLE: Vision-Language Detector Adaptation via online Cross-Modality Consistency
PROPOSAL: This experiment compares the performance of two test-time adaptation methods for a vision-language detector such as GLIP, one using online cross-modality consistency (CMC) loss to align visual features with text embeddings, and the other using a traditional self-training scheme with pseudo-labels generated on the fly. The CMC loss is defined as a cross-entropy loss between the mean-pooled visual features and the text embeddings, but with a regularization term that encourages the features and text embeddings to be consistent across different modalities. We hypothesize that the CMC method will adapt the detector more efficiently and effectively while preserving the pre-trained generalization capability.
CONTROLS: Baseline is given by the original GLIP detector without adaptation, ablation studies compare the CMC method with different components removed (e.g., regularization term, cross-entropy loss), and another control uses a traditional self-training scheme for comparison.
COST: 2500
PREDICTION: We expect the CMC method to outperform the self-training scheme in terms of detection accuracy and adaptation efficiency, especially when the detector is faced with scarce target data. TITLE: Regularized Online Adaptation for Vision-Language Detectors with Noisy Pseudo-Labels
PROPOSAL: This experiment investigates the effect of noisy pseudo-labels on the adaptation performance of vision-language detectors. We propose a regularized online adaptation method that masks the pseudo-labels from noisy images and adds a regularization term to the loss function to avoid overfitting. Specifically, we use a noise-aware masking strategy to suppress pseudo-labels with low confidence, and then optimize the detector using a penalized loss that rewards class-wise agreement between predictions and pseudo-labels. We hypothesize that this method will improve the robustness and generalization ability of vision-language detectors in scenarios with noisy pseudo-labels.

However, it might fail to adapt in tasks with extremely imbalanced target distributions, where the regularization term may not be able to capture the underlying relationships between classes.

TITLE: Relaxed Multi-Task Self-Supervised Learning for Vision-Language Detectors
PROPOSAL:  In this work, we leverage self-supervised learning to adapt a pre-trained vision-language detector to new target domains at test time. Concretely, we adapt Faster R-CNN and subsequent variants to multi-task training where presenting the detector with a mix of object detection and image-text matching tasks. Unlike traditional approaches that usually freeze the backbone network and only fine-tune the detector's head, our method relaxes this constraint and softly encourages the backbone network to update its parameters, but also to do so slowly and robustly to preserved pre-trained generalization. The mixing of tasks forces the detector to generate pseudo-labels more reliably; the slow and robust updates reduce overfitting; the overall process is formulated into a self-supervised loss that is minimizable via a single objective without any source data.
CONTROLS:

- Ablation: remove soft update and only fine-tune the head, or remove image-text matching task
COST: 480
PREDICTION: We expect this method to improve adaptation performance by 3-4\% mAP over traditional self-training methods, while reducing overfitting and resulting in more accurate pseudo-labels, but it might be hampered by the vanishing gradient problem when pseudo-labels are rare.

TITLE: Curriculum-Learned Online Pseudo-Label Correction
PROPOSAL: To address the challenge of high-quality pseudo-labels under noise and scarcity, we propose a curriculum-learned online pseudo-label correction mechanism. The mechanism is composed of two modules: a hard pseudo-label assigner, which selects a small batch of unlabeled images with high-quality pseudo-labels generated by the detector, and a soft correction module, which takes a small labeled training set and all the unlabeled images to correct the pseudo-labels via classification-based refinement under a guidance of curriculum learning. Curricula are learned on-the-fly to balance the correction quality and efficiency. The corrected pseudo-labels are then incorporated into the detector's training pipeline, leading to improved adaptation.

- Ablation: remove the hard pseudo-label assigner, or add a different pseudo-label correction strategy

PREDICTION: This mechanism is expected to enhance the mAP by 4-6\% on noisy and few-shot pseudo-label cases, but potentially over-correct the pseudo-labels resulting in degraded performance if not tuned carefully.

TITLE: Efficient Multi-View 3D Reconstruction with Appearance using Depth-Heatmap Voxel Grid (DHVG)
PROPOSAL: We propose DHVG, a compact 3D latent representation that jointly captures an object's geometry and view-dependent appearance by learning a sparse voxel grid where each voxel is represented by a depth value and a heat-map of appearance features. We use a Bidirectional Feature Propagation network to propagate features between voxels, enabling efficient learning and inference. Our model is trained end-to-end from 2D images to 3D reconstructions with appearance, without requiring heavy data preprocessing or a two-stage generation process.
CONTROLS: We compare DHVG to Structured Latents, Primitive-based Representations, and a strong baseline: Occupancy Layers.
COST: 384 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: DHVG outperforms existing methods in both geometric accuracy and view-dependent appearance, but may struggle with very high-resolution inputs or cases where the object's appearance varies greatly with viewpoint due to reflections or highlights, which may necessitate more sophisticated rendering.

TITLE: Accelerating DHVG with Render-to-Mesh and Closed-Loop Iterative Refinement
PROPOSAL: To improve the efficiency of DHVG and reduce computational overhead, we introduce two key components: (1) a render-to-mesh approach to facilitate high-quality surface normal estimation and image manipulation, and (2) a closed-loop iterative refinement mechanism that re-estimates DHVG's parameters and surface normals at multiple iterations. These innovations enable DHVG to adapt to challenging objects and improve accuracy without imposing significant computational burdens.
CONTROLS: We evaluate the impact of render-to-mesh and the closed-loop refinement on DHVG's accuracy, efficiency, and convergence.
COST: 3264 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The proposed components significantly accelerate DHVG's convergence rate while maintaining its accuracy, but may introduce difficulties in hyperparameter tuning due to their interactive nature.

ACTION: ADD 5
TITLE: Learning a Coherent Visual Appearance Representation using Hybrid LR-SR Images
PROPOSAL: We propose a novel data augmentation technique that leverages a deep learning-based hybrid low-resolution (LR) - super-resolution (SR) image synthesis framework to generate coherent appearance representations. By conditioning the SR network on the LR images, obtained from a facial/reflectance rendering process, we sample a diverse set of plausible HR images that preserve the hard-to-recover appearance effects. These simulated HR images are then used to augment the dataset for DHVG's training, effectively introducing a learning mechanism that incorporates view-dependent appearance and rich textures.
CONTROLS: We investigate the effect of this augmentation on DHVG's robustness against variations in viewpoint, texture, and appearance effects and assess whether the synthetic images can mitigate the limitations of real-world data.
COST: 3840 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The proposed image synthesis approach enables DHVG to generate more coherent and accurate appearance representations, especially for objects with rich textures and subtle shading effects.

TITLE: A Prior-Based 3D Reconstruction Approach for Illumination-Invariant Generation
PROPOSAL: We propose a novel prior-based 3D reconstruction approach that utilizes an explicit appearance prior to enhance DHVG's generative model and renderings. This prior is learned from a large dataset of textured, 3D meshes, where each mesh has associated textures and lighting condition annotations. By incorporating this prior into the DHVG framework, we can more accurately reconstruct objects from images under varying lighting conditions, achieving better color constancy and texture detail preservation.
CONTROLS: We compare our approach to the state-of-the-art methods, including NeRF and DHVG, on various real-world image datasets and 3D reconstruction benchmarks.
COST: 7480 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The prior-based approach yields significant improvements in illumination-invariant generation and color constancy, but may introduce additional computational overhead due to the learned prior's complexity and its training requirements.

PROPOSAL: We propose the first online, adaptive configuration optimization framework for multi-label image classification, called "Adaptive Learner" (AL). AL dynamically adjusts four core training components - augmentation, optimizer, learning-rate schedule, and loss function - every 5 epochs based on the evolving training state and the interactions among components. The adjustment process involves a neural network that takes the current training state as input and outputs the new configuration. We train the neural network to minimize a dynamic loss function that considers both the current and future validation performance. PROPOSAL: To efficiently explore the high-dimensional configuration space in the Adaptive Learner (AL) framework, we propose grouping the four core training components into categories based on their types and characteristics. TITLE: Exploring Knowledge Distillation for Efficient PTQ Training in 3D Reconstruction
PROPOSAL: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a technique that enables efficient training of smaller neural networks by transferring knowledge from a larger teacher network to a smaller student network. We will investigate the effectiveness of KD in PTQ frameworks for 3D reconstruction tasks. Specifically, we will train a smaller student network to mimic the behavior of a larger teacher network, which is quantized using PTQ, and evaluate its performance on various 3D reconstruction tasks. Our goal is to determine whether KD can accelerate PTQ training while preserving its accuracy.
CONTROLS: We will compare the performance of our distilled student network against the baseline teacher network, as well as two other variants: a naively trained student network with the same number of parameters as the teacher network, and a PTQ-trained student network without KD. 
COST: 56000
PREDICTION: We expect that KD will significantly accelerate PTQ training, allowing us to achieve better accuracy with fewer optimization iterations, but may introduce some degree of performance degradation due to the loss of information during distillation.
